title: The continuity map and classical sheaves, in detail
statement:
Let $X$ be a scheme and $F$ a sheaf of sets on $X_{\Proet}$ [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site]. Use the universes of [def-weil-size-convention]; all index categories below are small in the universe in which the colimits are formed [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit]. For module coefficients, fix a discrete commutative ring $\Lambda$ and its constant sheaf $\Lambda_X$, as in [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site]; module sheaves have the meaning of [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category].

1. **Presentations.** A *pro-étale affine presentation* is an affine object $U$ of $X_{\Proet}$, a small cofiltered category $I$, a diagram $i\mapsto U_i$ of affine schemes étale over $X$, and a specified isomorphism $U\cong\varprojlim_{i\in I}U_i$ of $X$-schemes, as in [sk-def-pe-morphisms]. For an arrow $a:j\to i$ write $u_a:U_j\to U_i$, and write $u_i:U\to U_i$ for the projections. The $U_i$ are objects of $X_{\Proet}$ because étale morphisms are weakly étale [det-pe-morphisms-etale-comparison]; the $u_a$ and $u_i$ are morphisms of that site.
2. **The continuity map.** The restriction maps $F(u_a):F(U_i)\to F(U_j)$ form a filtered diagram indexed by $I^{\mathrm{op}}$. The compatible maps $F(u_i)$ induce the unique map
$$c_{F,(U_i)}:\varinjlim_{i\in I^{\mathrm{op}}}F(U_i)\longrightarrow F(U),\qquad [i,s]\longmapsto F(u_i)(s).$$
It is natural in $F$. The notation retains the presentation, since the source of the map depends on that presentation.
3. **Classical sheaves.** $F$ is *classical* if $c_{F,(U_i)}$ is bijective for every such presentation. For a sheaf of $\Lambda_X$-modules, take the colimit in $\Lambda$-modules, with the $\Lambda$-actions on sections induced by the canonical maps $\Lambda\to\Lambda_X(V)$. The resulting map is $\Lambda$-linear. Such a module sheaf is *classical* if every resulting continuity map is an isomorphism of $\Lambda$-modules; equivalently its underlying sheaf of sets is classical.
4. **Complexes.** A cochain complex of $\Lambda_X$-module sheaves, or an object $K$ of $D(X_{\Proet},\Lambda)$ [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], is *classical* if every cohomology sheaf $H^q(K)$ is classical. This depends only on the isomorphism class in the derived category.

When $X$ is affine, the objects $U$ admitting these presentations are exactly the affine ind-étale objects of [def-weil-pbc-ind-etale-basis], with ind-étale understood as in [def-weil-pbc-ind-etale-algebra]. For general $X$ the inverse-limit formulation of [sk-def-pe-morphisms] is the definition used here.

proof.text: The presentations are taken in the fixed universe [def-weil-size-convention]. By [det-pe-morphisms-etale-comparison], each étale $U_i\to X$ is weakly étale, hence an object of the site [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site]. The presentation clause of [sk-def-pe-morphisms] supplies the affine stages and the $X$-morphism transitions. Its arrows are all $X$-morphisms, so all projections and transitions are site arrows. Contravariant functoriality gives $F(u_j)\circ F(u_a)=F(u_i)$ from $u_a\circ u_j=u_i$. The functor laws for the transition maps and these identities give a diagram on the filtered category $I^{\mathrm{op}}$ and a cocone.

source.place: first paragraph: functoriality and site arrows

proof.text: Construct the set colimit as the disjoint union of the $F(U_i)$ modulo the equivalence relation generated by $(i,s)\sim(j,F(u_a)(s))$. For any cocone of maps $\mu_i:F(U_i)\to T$, the rule $[i,s]\mapsto\mu_i(s)$ respects the generating pairs by cocone compatibility. It therefore descends to the quotient, and it is the unique map with these composites on the summands, since every class has a representative. This verifies the colimit universal property [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit]. Apply it to the cocone from step 1 to obtain $c([i,s])=F(u_i)(s)$. For a sheaf morphism $\alpha:F\to G$, the two composites applied to $[i,s]$ are $\alpha_U(F(u_i)(s))$ and $G(u_i)(\alpha_{U_i}(s))$, equal by naturality of $\alpha$. This proves naturality of $c$.

source.place: Tag 002U, section-limit-sets: quotient construction and its universal property; blueprint continuity-map proof, first paragraph

proof.text: For any small filtered diagram of $\Lambda$-modules, apply [lem-weil-pbc-ring-modules-grothendieck-abelian] with $R=\Lambda$ to obtain its module colimit $M$. Construct its set colimit $L$ by the quotient in step 2. There is a comparison map from $L$ to the underlying set of $M$, sending $[i,s]$ to $\iota_i(s)$. By clause (1) of [lem-weil-pbc-filtered-colimit-modules-elementwise], this map is surjective. By clause (2), equal images of $[i,s]$ and $[j,t]$ become equal after arrows to a common stage, so they are already equal in the quotient $L$. The comparison is therefore a bijection compatible with the structure maps. This proves the particular forgetful-colimit comparison used here without assuming that evaluation of arbitrary sheaf colimits is sectionwise.

Restriction of scalars along $\Lambda\to\Lambda_X(V)$ gives each section module its $\Lambda$-action. The semilinearity in [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category] and compatibility of the constant sections with restriction give $F(u)(\lambda s)=\lambda F(u)(s)$. Hence the transition maps form a filtered diagram of $\Lambda$-modules and all $F(u_i)$ are $\Lambda$-linear and form a module cocone. Apply step 3 to this diagram. Its induced map from the module colimit [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit] agrees, under step 3's bijection, with the set map of step 2, because their values on every $[i,s]$ agree. A bijective linear map has linear inverse: apply the map to the desired additivity and scalar identities of the inverse and use injectivity. Thus classicality of the module sheaf is equivalent to classicality of its underlying sheaf of sets.

source.place: second paragraph: linearity and equivalence of the two conditions

proof.text: If $\alpha:F\xrightarrow{\sim}G$ is an isomorphism of sheaves, its components $\alpha_{U_i}$ and $\alpha_U$ are bijections, and $[i,s]\mapsto[i,\alpha_{U_i}(s)]$ has inverse induced by $\alpha^{-1}$. The naturality identity of step 2 therefore identifies the two continuity maps by bijections on their sources and targets. One is bijective if and only if the other is. For module sheaves, the components and their inverses are linear, hence their maps on the module colimits are inverse linear maps; the naturality square then identifies the module continuity maps by module isomorphisms.

source.place: third paragraph: invariance of sheaf classicality under isomorphism

proof.text: Use [def-weil-abstract-derived-category] with the abelian category of $\Lambda_X$-module sheaves [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. It supplies $H^q:D(\mathcal A)\to\mathcal A$ factoring the cochain cohomology functors. For an isomorphism $f:K\to L$ with inverse $g$, functoriality gives $H^q(g)H^q(f)=1$ and $H^q(f)H^q(g)=1$. Thus the cohomology sheaves are isomorphic, and step 5 makes the predicate 'all $H^q$ are classical' invariant. A quasi-isomorphism already induces these isomorphisms by its definition, so the cochain and derived formulations agree.

source.place: Tag 05RT, lemma-acyclic, and Tag 05RU, definition-unbounded-derived-category; blueprint proof, third paragraph

proof.text: For the reverse implication, unfold the recorded proAffineEtale presentation, enlarge its index from u to u+1 using MorphismProperty.pro_of_univLE, and lift the affine étale stages and structure maps to X.ProEt. The cone has vertex U. Over.forget reflects its limit since a cofiltered index is connected. For the forward implication, apply global sections to the given affine stages and cone; étaleness of the resulting ring maps follows from the affine ring-map characterization.

source.place: Last sentence, with affine-base scope made explicit; Stacks Morphisms Tag 02GJ (lemma-etale-characterize), Algebra Tag 00U1 (definition-etale), and Limits Tag 01YW (lemma-directed-inverse-system-affine-schemes-has-limit); ring/algebra colimit comparison and limit-over-X check by the displayed universal properties

proof.text: Identify each affine scheme naturally with the spectrum of its global sections. Transport the given scheme limit along these identifications and reflect it through the fully faithful Spec functor. Taking opposites gives the colimit property of the global-sections cocone. Its structure maps commute by the Over equations, so it exhibits the vertex structure map as ind-etale with index in u+1. No separately chosen ring colimit is needed.

source.place: Last sentence, with affine-base scope made explicit; Stacks Morphisms Tag 02GJ (lemma-etale-characterize), Algebra Tag 00U1 (definition-etale), and Limits Tag 01YW (lemma-directed-inverse-system-affine-schemes-has-limit); ring/algebra colimit comparison and limit-over-X check by the displayed universal properties

proof.text: Apply [lem-pe-ind-etale-small-index] to shrink this filtered étale ring presentation to universe u. The recorded RingHom.IndEtale.iff_ind_etale and proAffineEtale_iff_appTop identify the affine vertex morphism as proAffineEtale. Transport this property across the supplied isomorphism of site objects by cancellation of the isomorphism. This proves exactly the claimed equivalence, with the original affine-base scope.

- Step 1: clause 1 of det-pe-morphisms-etale-comparison gives étale ⇒ weakly étale, and the transition and projection maps are X-morphisms as in sk-def-pe-morphisms. The contravariant order F(u_j)∘F(u_a)=F(u_i) is correct.
- Step 2: the quotient colimit of sets (Stacks 002U) with its universal property and naturality; correct.
- Step 3: the two Mathlib-leaf module-colimit nodes give a bijection between the set colimit and the underlying set of the module colimit; correct.
- Step 4: semilinearity gives the Λ-action and Λ-linearity, and a bijective linear map has a linear inverse; correct.
- Steps 5-6: classicality is invariant under sheaf isomorphism, and H^r on D(A) factors through Q, so it depends only on the derived isomorphism class; correct.
- Steps 7-9: the affine identification. The étale ring-map criterion is used in both directions, the ring colimit gets its R-algebra structure (this uses filteredness and nonemptiness), and Spec of the colimit is shown to be the limit over X; correct.
